# Original video fixture

`mjpeg.mov` is the Apache-2.0 synthetic fixture from `zig/lib/video/testdata`,
generated by its `scripts/generate_mjpeg_fixtures.py`; see the original hashed receipt
and generator for source and oracle provenance. This small copy is embedded
inside the inference package for presentation sampling/HTTP adapter tests.

`mjpeg-vfr.mov` preserves the original compressed packets and total duration while
replacing `stts` with eight durations: `[1024,1024,1024,1024,8192,8192,6144,6144]`
at timescale 16384. `tools/embeddinggemma2/video_policy_qualification.py` creates
it from the pinned pretrained fixture; its Python contract test verifies this
embedded copy byte-for-byte. The native model test verifies every compressed
packet matches the CFR source. It is a synthetic Apache-2.0 derivative.

`h264-frameonly.mp4` copies the Apache-2.0 generated pretrained video fixture
`tools/embeddinggemma2/testdata/video/video-h264.mp4` (SHA-256
`35c72f117cbf9f56064f69ca4b82217acb51b8b7c34953829917d11e4f359676`).
Its pinned processor/decode provenance is recorded by that directory's
`video-oracle.json`. It exercises independent VideoToolbox/Metal production
before model execution and queue abandonment with actual CoreVideo imports.


`closed.ts` and `bframes.ts` are generated by the independently reproducible
`zig/lib/media/scripts/generate_ts_fixtures.py`. Their corresponding MP4 originals
are copied from `schedule-closed.mp4` and `decode-bframes.mp4` in `lib/video`.
The model suite checks identical logical sampling, preflight plans and prepared
F32 patch hashes across containers. `transport-validation/corpus.json` pins
those four synthetic clips and two query texts for pretrained reference/vector,
retrieval and exact prompt-token comparisons. This is reference preservation;
it supplies no application relevance judgments or general TS conformance claim.

`closed-split.ts` and `bframes-split.ts` are generated by
`zig/lib/media/scripts/generate_ts_split_fixtures.py`. They preserve the original
compressed access-unit bytes/clocks while splitting prefixes, parameter sets and
slices into timestamp-free continuation PES. The model producer compares their
prepared F32 patch hashes against original MP4 and aligned TS. Independent
packet/picture evidence and FFprobe's timestamp-loss limitation are recorded in
`zig/lib/media/testdata/transport/assembly-validation`. This continuation does
not rerun pretrained checkpoint inference for the split-layout files.

`live-fragmented.mp4` is an exact copy of the synthetic Apache-2.0
`zig/lib/media/testdata/fragmented.mp4` and
`zig/lib/video/testdata/live/fragmented.mp4` fixture (SHA-256
`8b0d6caa76acfa98258536bce04d1ae058ba2ff2c4dcfb4e109cd289bea8d8be`).
Its existing generator and FFprobe receipts live in those libraries. The file
contains six one-second moof/mdat fragments, 60 H.264 samples at 10 FPS and native
1/10240 clocks. Its B-picture presentation timeline begins at 0.2 seconds and
ends at 6.2 seconds. Streaming model tests use six one-second source windows,
explicit output/commit retry and an authenticated server-withheld-tail gate.


`live-encrypted.bin` is an exact copy of
`zig/lib/media/testdata/hls/aes-stream/media.bin`: OpenSSL AES-128 CBC/PKCS7
encryption of `live-fragmented.mp4[797:]` with public fixture key bytes 00..0f
and sequence IV 10. The media fixture manifest records its tool, command and
source/plaintext/ciphertext hashes. Runtime uses native Zig decryption; the
checkpoint streaming gate compares against buffered plaintext HLS windows.


`ll-part-half.m4s` and `ll-parent-2s.mp4` copy the media qualification fixtures
in `zig/lib/media/testdata/hls/`. FFmpeg packet-copy remuxing creates a half-second
part and two-second parent moofs from `live-fragmented.mp4`; native DTS/PTS,
duration, size, sync and encoded SHA-256 agree with all 60 source packets.
`ll-parent-2s.json` records commands, tool, source/fixture hashes and packet
provenance. The checkpoint gate consumes the part before a complete parent,
then compares six streamed window vectors with buffered full-clip HLS inference.
